briefings.title: Draghi: France is Far From Becoming a Euro-Area Crisis
briefings.tldr: Former ECB President Mario Draghi dismissed fears of a French debt-driven euro area crisis while warning that global trade fragmentation requires Europe to rapidly forge new economic coalitions with partners like India and Canada.

briefings.title: Economics after Certainty
briefings.tldr: Economic policy can no longer rely on predictability, as repeated structural shocks, geopolitical fragmentation, and rapid technological shifts like generative AI have exposed the limits of equilibrium thinking and traditional forecasting.

briefings.title: Fed’s Christopher Waller Talks Higher Yields, Inflation | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller noted that a surge in long-term US Treasury yields is helping cool interest-rate-sensitive sectors like housing and autos, functioning as a de facto rate hike.

briefings.title: AI’s Giant Money Loop Is Feeling Very 2008 | Big Take
briefings.tldr: The AI infrastructure boom is being fueled by circular global capital flows—with foreign chip-maker savings recycling back into US markets—creating global imbalances and economic risks reminiscent of the run-up to the 2008 financial crisis.

briefings.title: Trade Wars, Fighting Corruption and Rethinking Globalization | Leaders with Francine Lacqua
briefings.tldr: Global trade is facing unprecedented disruption and fragmentation reminiscent of the 1930s, driven by geopolitical tensions, shifting subsidies, and protectionism.

briefings.title: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem Talks Fed Rates | Bloomberg Talks

people.name: Alberto Musalem
people.role: President, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
people.organization: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

organizations: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem stated that interest rates should increase further over the next six to nine months to sustainably return inflation to the central bank’s 2% target within 18 months, pointing to persistent demand pressures and strong economic growth.

briefings.title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon Talks AI Boom, Bond Selloff | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that relentless global government borrowing and AI capital expenditure will create long-term inflation and credit risks, while urging policymakers to prioritize growth-oriented structural reforms like deregulation over ad hoc taxes.

briefings.title: JPMorgan's Dimon on Financing the AI Boom
briefings.tldr: Jamie Dimon warned that Anthropic's Mythos model has increased global cybersecurity risks tenfold, while discussing global capital constraints, data center development, and the risks of discriminatory bank taxation in the UK.

briefings.title: Suno's Mikey Shulman on the AI Music Landscape
briefings.tldr: Suno CEO Mikey Shulman discusses the company's evolution from a controversial generative music tool into a broader "creative entertainment" platform, detailing industry partnerships, upcoming speech products, and a vision for deeply interactive fan-artist music experiences.

briefings.title: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin & Carnegie Mellon President Farnam Jahanian Talk Donation, New Campus |...
briefings.tldr: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin is committing a record $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University—with $2 billion funding a new campus in Miami and $1 billion supporting the main Pittsburgh campus, including naming the Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science—to pioneer a tech-forward, interdisciplinary model for higher education focused on return on investment and grand societal challenges.

briefings.title: Griffin Gives $3 Billion to Carnegie Mellon for Miami Campus
briefings.tldr: Citadel founder Ken Griffin is donating a record-breaking $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University—doubling his total lifetime contributions to roughly $5.7 billion—with a significant portion funding a new CMU campus in Miami designed around a pioneering, interdisciplinary model for higher education.

briefings.title: Pershing Square founder and CEO Bill Ackman Talks Howard Hughes Plans, IPOs and Anthropic |...
briefings.tldr: Pershing Square founder and CEO Bill Ackman discussed his strategy for Howard Hughes Corp., the capitalization of insurance venture Vantage, Pershing Square USA's market discount, AI frontier models, and a new brain-care institute inspired by his daughter's recovery.

briefings.title: Microsoft AI CEO, Mustafa Suleyman on Why Industry Needs a 'Red Line' for AI
briefings.tldr: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman argues that the AI industry must establish a firm "red line" requiring proof of control before deployment, warning against dangerous trends in model welfare and open-ended autonomous agent swarms.

briefings.title: AI Pioneer Fei-Fei Li Talks AI Safety, Competition with China | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: World Labs CEO Fei-Fei Li discussed the development of spatial intelligence and "world models" like the company's new Atlas model, emphasizing the need for robust ecosystems and human-centric governance to manage AI's dual-edged nature.

briefings.title: Howard Marks Flags the Uncertainty in AI Investing
briefings.tldr: Markets have been dominated by optimists driven by strong economic aggregates, the TINA trade, and AI enthusiasm, though this requires heightened investor caution.

briefings.title: IMF MD on the Global Economic Outlook
briefings.tldr: Global economic growth is proving resilient at around 3%, supported by positive AI demand and emerging market strength, but faces persistent risks from sticky inflation, rising debt-servicing costs, and AI-driven financial stability concerns.

briefings.title: Qatar, Brookfield on Trade, Investment and Competition

people.name: Faisal bin Thani bin Faisal Al-Thani

briefings.tldr: Despite global uncertainties and regional instability, Qatar continues to maintain strong GDP growth and attract record foreign investment, while partnerships like Brookfield and the Qatar Investment Authority are scaling up local AI infrastructure and energy-to-compute projects.

briefings.title: QatarEnergy on Energy Security and Supply

people.name: Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi
people.role: Minister of State for Energy Affairs, Qatar

briefings.tldr: QatarEnergy is navigating an unprecedented total shutdown of its oil and gas facilities due to disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz, cutting 17% of its LNG capacity.

briefings.title: The Infrastructure of Intelligence: NVIDIA and OpenAI on a Decade of Building Frontier AI

people.name: Ian Buck
people.role: VP of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, NVIDIA

briefings.tldr: AI infrastructure has evolved rapidly from single-GPU nodes to gigawatt-scale data centers, driven by continuous scaling laws and deep co-design partnerships like the decade-long collaboration between NVIDIA and OpenAI.

briefings.title: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan Talks Trading Revenue, AI Safety | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan expects third-quarter trading revenue to be relatively flat compared to an exceptionally strong prior year, while warning that the rapid pace of artificial intelligence development requires deliberate safety guardrails and careful corporate deployment.

briefings.title: Barclays CEO CS Venkatakrishnan Talks AI Development & Inflation | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: Barclays CEO CS Venkatakrishnan warned that persistent inflation, rising global debt-to-GDP ratios, and heavy tech-related debt supply are pressuring bond markets, while emphasizing that AI serves as an efficiency tool requiring workforce reskilling rather than a total replacement of fundamental banking infrastructure.

briefings.title: David Sacks: Anthropic, OpenAI Should Slow AI If Deemed Necessary

people.name: David Sacks
people.role: Chair, President's Council of Advisors on Science & Technology
people.organization: President's Council of Advisors on Science & Technology

organizations: President's Council of Advisors on Science & Technology
briefings.tldr: David Sacks argues that frontier AI labs Anthropic and OpenAI do not need new government regulations or antitrust waivers to slow down development for safety, asserting they already possess the market lead, incentives, and existing product liability laws to manage risks themselves.

briefings.title: AI Industry Has Done 'Terrible Job' of Communicating Benefits, Says Sam Altman
briefings.tldr: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman admitted the AI industry has done a "terrible job" communicating technology benefits to the public while discussing the release of GPT-6 (Astra), which hit cyber-critical thresholds by autonomously finding zero-day exploits.

briefings.title: IMF Chief Praises Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole Speech
briefings.tldr: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva praised Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech for its clarity on price stability, while warning that high global debt levels and rapid technological innovation complicate central bank efforts to manage inflation.

briefings.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on the AI Boom in South Korea
briefings.tldr: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced a major $500 billion business partnership with South Korea's SK Group at an AI summit in San Francisco, while highlighting critical supply chain constraints, the necessity of open AI models for cybersecurity, and the massive future expansion of the semiconductor industry.

briefings.title: Fireside Chat with Yann LeCun, Executive Chairman of AMI Labs | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Yann LeCun argues that current Large Language Models (LLMs) are fundamentally incapable of achieving true intelligence or understanding the physical world; his new venture, AMI Labs, is developing "World Models" (JEPA) to bridge this gap, enabling robots and autonomous systems to learn from observation and predict the consequences of their actions.

briefings.title: Former Fed Vice Chair Lael Brainard Talks Warsh's First Fed Meeting | Bloomberg Talks

people.name: Lael Brainard
people.role: Former Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve

briefings.tldr: In his debut meeting as Federal Reserve Chair, Kevin Warsh introduced a hawkish shift marked by dot-plot projections pointing to potential rate hikes, though former Fed Vice Chair Lael Brainard suggests Warsh is quietly positioning for policy flexibility through new task forces and a softer stance on the 2% inflation target.

briefings.title: Chevron CEO Wirth on Energy  Market Volatility
briefings.tldr: While tactical supply-and-demand responses have temporarily buffered the global energy market from geopolitical conflicts, Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warns that declining inventories could trigger severe market tightness by July or August.

briefings.title: Broadcom CEO on the Biggest AI Chip Bets
briefings.tldr: Broadcom is prioritizing massive organic growth over mergers and acquisitions, leveraging custom AI silicon partnerships with Google and OpenAI to drive record-breaking revenues.

briefings.title: Databricks CEO on Unifying Data & AI Agents
briefings.tldr: Following a $5 billion funding round at a $134 billion valuation, Databricks is experiencing unprecedented, agent-driven growth and is expanding into the cybersecurity market with its new product, Lakewatch.

briefings.title: Meta AI Chief Wang on Winning the Race in AI
briefings.tldr: At Bloomberg Tech 2026, Meta’s Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang discussed the company's aggressive transition toward frontier AI capabilities, highlighting the success of its "Muse Spark" model and its upcoming competitive "entree" model.

briefings.title: VC Haun on Investing in the Frontiers of AI Agents
briefings.tldr: Haun Ventures has launched a new $1 billion fund targeting the "new economy" and the future of finance, focusing heavily on building 24/7 global financial infrastructure and cryptographic rails designed specifically for autonomous AI agents.

briefings.title: Musk vs Altlman & Taylor Swift Trademarks | Bloomberg Law
briefings.tldr: Elon Musk is seeking to unwind OpenAI's for-profit conversion in a high-stakes trial alleging the "theft" of a non-profit charity, while Taylor Swift is pioneering a novel legal strategy using trademark law to combat AI deepfakes.

briefings.title: Will Social Media Bans Actually Work? | Bloomberg Tech: Asia 4/24/2026
briefings.tldr: Governments worldwide are shifting toward hardline age-based restrictions for social media to combat youth mental health crises and platform addiction, moving beyond parental controls to treat digital access with the same regulatory weight as alcohol and tobacco.

briefings.title: Bloomberg This Weekend | Standstill in Strait, Warsh Heads to the Hill, Blue Origin Blastoff
briefings.tldr: Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have reached a critical impasse as Iran maintains its blockade, prompting the Trump administration to deploy special envoy Steve Witkoff to Pakistan for high-stakes negotiations while simultaneously threatening to target Iranian infrastructure.

briefings.title: Weekly Washington Policy Pulse: War Powers, Iran Defense, Warsh Nod (April 13, 2026) | Balance...
briefings.tldr: Congress enters a high-velocity legislative window ahead of the 2026 midterms, prioritizing a two-part reconciliation strategy to fund the Department of Homeland Security and a massive $80–$200 billion defense supplemental targeting Iranian threats.

briefings.title: Dentro de la Megafábrica Stargate de OpenAI con Sam Altman | The Circuit
briefings.tldr: Project Stargate is a historic $100 billion to $500 billion AI infrastructure initiative in Abilene, Texas, led by OpenAI, SoftBank, and Oracle to build the world’s largest computing clusters and accelerate the path to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI).

briefings.title: Inside Arm’s AI Pivot: From Smartphones to the Cloud | Bloomberg Tech: Europe 4/10/2026
briefings.tldr: Arm is executing a massive strategic pivot from licensing smartphone chip designs to becoming a primary producer of high-end AI silicon, targeting a data center market opportunity projected to exceed $100 billion.

briefings.title: LGT’s Prince Max Urges Global Asset Diversification

people.name: Prince Max von und zu Liechtenstein

briefings.tldr: To navigate escalating geopolitical instability and the rapid onset of AI, Prince Max urges investors to prioritize global geographic diversification and integrate long-term "purpose" into family governance to ensure multi-generational survival.

briefings.title: HPS CEO Kapnick on the Next Wave in Private Credit
briefings.tldr: Private credit is undergoing a multi-decade structural expansion driven by bank retrenchment and massive infrastructure/AI funding needs, where success will increasingly depend on "scaled" players capable of managing a return to historical default norms through sophisticated risk workouts.

briefings.title: KKR CEO Nuttall on Dealmaking & Investment Outlook
briefings.tldr: KKR Co-CEO Scott Nuttall anticipates a "K-shaped" divergence in the private equity industry, where firms practicing disciplined "linear deployment" will thrive while those who over-leveraged during the bull market face consolidation.

briefings.title: Temasek CEO Shares Investor's View on Private Markets
briefings.tldr: Temasek is rebalancing its \$340 billion portfolio toward a 50/50 split between liquid and illiquid assets to maintain agility amid frequent macro shocks, prioritizing AI adoption and global equities while navigating high interest rates and geopolitical volatility.

briefings.title: Ares CEO on Access & Risks in Private Markets
briefings.tldr: Ares CEO Michael Arougheti argues that the private markets are entering a "winner-take-most" era where scale drives performance, dismisses "irresponsible" predictions of high default rates, and views persistent inflation as a net positive for private credit returns.

briefings.title: BAM, Invesco CEOs Discuss Private Market Opportunities
briefings.tldr: The private market is undergoing a structural shift toward the individual wealth channel—a market twice the size of the institutional sector—driven by demand for infrastructure, AI-related digital assets, and high-yield private credit.
